subject: Inference execution evidence and egress controls — DataOps follow-up
body_plain:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@dataops.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: security@dataops.com
Date: Fri, 30 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Where does Redwood actually execute inference? Evidence for export controls

Hi Marcus,

Thanks for the demo last week. Our security team is doing a quick intake: can you confirm where Redwood executes inference for production requests and whether any customer data ever leaves the target region? Specifically:

- Which cloud regions are used for hosted inference (US, EU, APAC)?
- Do you use subprocessors that may be outside those regions (KMS, logging, metrics)?
- Any intermediate handoffs or caching that could cause cross-border egress?

We need an evidence pack (diagram + brief answers) for our procurement review.

Best,
Elena
Security Operations
DataOps Inc.

----
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@dataops.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Jun 2028 11:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Where does Redwood actually execute inference? Evidence for export controls

Elena —

Appreciate the clear list. High level answers below; attaching a simple execution-diagram and our SOC 2 excerpts that call out network controls. I’ll also loop in Neha for the execution/subprocessor detail and Jordan for procurement evidence.

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- Hosted (Redwood API): we run inference in customer-selected multi-region endpoints. By default US and EU regions are available; APAC is available in select markets.
- Routing: requests are routed to region-local clusters when the route policy specifies region affinity. If a customer chooses EU-only execution we pin to EU clusters and disable cross-region fallbacks.
- Subprocessors: KMS, metrics ingestion, observability traces exist as separate services; most have region-specific endpoints but a small set of management/control-plane services are US-based.
- Caching/KV: we use ephemeral KV caches colocated with inference nodes; prefixes and KV shards do not persist beyond the request TTL unless customer opts in to longer cache.
- Deletion: customers can request immediate purge of model context and cached prefixes; standard retention for non-persistent telemetry is 30 days unless contract specifies otherwise.

Attachments: redwood_inference_geo_diagram.png, SOC2_AIC_excerpts.pdf

Next steps: Neha will enumerate subprocessors and exact endpoints, and we can provide a signed attestation if required.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin | Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@dataops.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 01 Jul 2028 08:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Where does Redwood actually execute inference? Evidence for export controls

Hi Elena —

Adding the technical breakdown you requested. I’ll keep answers concise and label where evidence is available.

1) Regions and exact compute sites
- Hosted API: customers can select from these compute regions: us-west-2 (Oregon), us-east-1 (N. Virginia), eu-west-1 (Ireland), eu-central-1 (Frankfurt), ap-southeast-1 (Singapore; limited availability), ap-northeast-1 (Tokyo; pilot).
- For Dedicated and Private customers we support on-prem and VPC deployments; those executions are fully inside customer-controlled networks.

Evidence: redwood_inference_geo_diagram.png (shows routing & region endpoints).

2) Subprocessors and potential cross-border endpoints
- KMS: customer-managed KMS is supported (recommended). By default we use a cloud KMS regional endpoint; management plane calls (key rotation alerts, audit logs) originate from our US control plane.
- Observability (metrics/traces): primary ingestion endpoints are regional; aggregated analytics and long-term retention is in US buckets for aggregated dashboards.
- Storage (checkpointing, logs): inference runtime checkpoints ephemeral state to region-local ephemeral storage. Long-term logs (audit, billing) are stored in encrypted buckets and replicated based on customer contract.

Evidence: attached subprocessor inventory (subprocessor_inventory.csv) with endpoints and host locations. SOC2_AIC_excerpts.pdf references controls around encryption and access control.

3) Caching and KV behavior (where data can touch)
- KV cache: located on the same cluster as the inference nodes in the elected region. Cache TTL default = 0 (no persistence) for standard API calls; longer TTLs only on customer request.
- Prefix caching (shared across requests): only enabled with explicit opt-in and designed for datasets customers choose to persist; administrators opt into region of persistence.

4) Cross-border fallbacks and automated routing
- By default we will not route outside the customer-selected region for requests flagged as region-restricted. There are automated fallback policies (e.g., to a compatible model variant in another region) that are only enabled if the customer permits cross-region fallback in their routing policy.

5) Deletion and purge timelines
- Model context purge: immediate upon request; we surface an API: POST /v1/customers/{id}/purge-context which returns job id and completion timestamp.
- Audit logs/billing: retained for 30 days by default; can be extended via contract.

If you want, we can produce a one-page signed attestation describing the above and listing our subprocessors and region endpoints.

—Neha Kapoor
Senior Technical Product Manager, Redwood Inference

Thanks Neha — this is exactly what we needed. A couple of follow-ups: 

- Can you confirm whether any management/control-plane logs ever include unredacted request payloads? Our requirement is that control-plane telemetry never carries full request bodies.
- For the SOC2 excerpts: can you highlight which sections correspond to network segregation and key management?
- One more ask: is there an option to enforce EU-only processing and have subprocessor endpoints contractually restricted to EU hosts (i.e., no US-based aggregation for analytics)?

If you can email the one-page attestation and a callout list for the SOC2 pages we’ll add it to procurement.

Best,
Elena
